live.instructions:
Chart authoring:
- Every field-bearing semantic role names a data key: category/values for column, bar, line, area, and pie; x/y for scatter; category/values/stepKind for waterfall. Count values intentionally omit a value field. Series and encoding fields must also exist in the same rows.
- Choose one chart type for the question: column/bar for categorical comparison, line/area for ordered trends, scatter for relationships, pie sparingly for part-to-whole, and waterfall for an ordered balance bridge.
- A waterfall has one measure and ordered stepKind values: optional first start, one or more signed changes, optional subtotals, and a final total. Subtotal and total amounts are null; the compiler calculates their balances. Do not add series or aggregation. Value labels default outside bars, and focus: "changes" shows large balances as points.
- Use long values with an optional series field, wide values with explicit fields, or count values. Aggregation belongs in the value role.
- Column and bar support grouped or stacked multi-series arrangements. Area charts stack by default and support normalization.
- Prefer native labels and references; use annotations for authored explanatory text.
- Axes, color/size legends, and line points accept true for default settings, false to hide, or an options object that enables them. Omission keeps defaults. Stack totals use a boolean. Do not add display to these objects.
- Column and bar charts with long, wide, or count values, and all area charts, use linear value scales. Their inferred domains include zero, while an explicit domain excluding zero produces a warning. Base-10 log roles and explicit log domains require positive finite values; use line, scatter, or ranged columns and bars.
- For chronological annual trends, use "YYYY" strings, set category.scale to { "type": "utc" }, and use category.format or categoryAxis.format "%Y". Do not invent dates. Categorical years may stay band; UTC numbers are Unix milliseconds.
- Set config.locale to the chart's language for non-English text. It controls formatting and regional character forms; use ja for Japanese or ko for Korean, including Han-only labels.
- Let themes style by default. Use color domains/ranges and themeOverrides only when they convey intentional meaning. A scalar color may provide light and dark members; a theme palette or continuous range provides one complete array per authored scheme. themeOverrides require a Creator or Pro plan and are rejected at render, not at validation.
- Use the same ChartDocument for validation, rendering, and saving: version, config, data, and optional presentation/size/output. Document version must match config.version. Prefer the smallest clear definition.

MCP workflow:
- Use get_examples when needed. Use get_schema with chart_type for the exact field contract; never discover a field by probing validate_chart for errors.
- The szum://schema and szum://llms-txt resources carry the same schema and the full authoring reference for clients that read MCP resources.
- Validate each generated or changed chart input once before rendering, saving, or updating. Do not revalidate unchanged input; a successful render preflights it for later saves or updates. Errors block; warnings require explicit user approval for the exact chart input. Rendering may add layout warnings to the semantic findings before an action proceeds. Suggestions do not block. A suggestedDocument is a complete, validated replacement. Review the proposed changes before using it; validate again only if you modify it. Validation is free and fast.
- Preview with render_chart. Offer to save once after the finished preview; do not repeat the offer during revisions. Save only when the user asks.
- Follow saved-chart tool scopes. Delete explicitly. Hide internals.

tools.name: render_chart
tools.title: Render chart
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to preview or generate a chart. Validate each generated or changed chart input once before rendering, saving, or updating. Do not revalidate unchanged input; a successful render preflights it for later saves or updates. Errors block; warnings require explicit user approval for the exact chart input. Rendering may add layout warnings to the semantic findings before an action proceeds. Suggestions do not block. A suggestedDocument is a complete, validated replacement. Review the proposed changes before using it; validate again only if you modify it. Stores a 1 hour preview and returns public image URLs. Authenticated previews use the account's render allowance, and each image produced from a returned URL is another render. Anonymous previews are complimentary; their images use the anonymous image allowance.

request.description: Complete current ChartDocument JSON with version, config, and data, plus optional presentation, size, and output. Use the same document for validation, rendering, and saving; version must match config.version. Semantic field roles must match row keys. Chronological annual values use YYYY strings on an explicit UTC scale. Column and bar charts with long, wide, or count values, and all area charts, use linear value scales. Their inferred domains include zero, while an explicit domain excluding zero produces a warning. Base-10 log roles and explicit log domains require positive finite values; use line, scatter, or ranged columns and bars.

tools.name: save_chart
tools.title: Save chart
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to permanently save and publish a Szum chart document. Validate each generated or changed chart input once before rendering, saving, or updating. Do not revalidate unchanged input; a successful render preflights it for later saves or updates. Errors block; warnings require explicit user approval for the exact chart input. Rendering may add layout warnings to the semantic findings before an action proceeds. Suggestions do not block. A suggestedDocument is a complete, validated replacement. Review the proposed changes before using it; validate again only if you modify it. Supply one idempotencyKey per intended chart and reuse it for retries. Returns permanent public Image and Embed URLs plus Edit and Studio links; requires authentication and saved-chart storage.

tools.name: get_examples
tools.title: Get example charts
tools.description: Get complete Szum documents for validation, rendering, or saving, with guidance on when to use each pattern. No filters returns one starter per chart type. Any filter searches the complete catalog; all supplied filters intersect. Most data is illustrative; the Vinyl waterfall cites RIAA reports. Empty matches mean no example satisfies every filter; remove a filter to broaden the search.

purpose.description: Filter by the primary chart question. Distribution means categorical frequencies, not automatic histogram binning. Range means bounded values, time spans, or uncertainty.

features.description: Return examples teaching every selected feature. Annotations explain data; references mark fixed values or statistics; ranges encode start/end values; intervals show lower/upper bounds around scatter observations.

example_id.description: Retrieve an exact ID from an earlier example result. Intersects any other supplied filters.

request.description: Complete current ChartDocument. get_schema returns its JSON Schema.

tools.name: get_schema
tools.title: Get chart document schema
tools.description: Use this before authoring an unfamiliar field instead of probing validate_chart for errors. Returns the JSON Schema for the whole Szum document, covering config, data, presentation, size, and output, with every referenced definition included. Pass chart_type to keep only that family's config variants; omitting it returns every family and is much larger. Generated value lists are summarized rather than enumerated; validate_chart remains the authority.

chart_type.description: Keep only the config variants for this chart type. Pass it whenever the family is known.
